How do you form the comparative of an adjective?
column2: Drop the long vowel, prefix ا, put sukuun on the second letter and fatha on the third: the أَفْعَل pattern.
column3: كْبير → أَكْبَر; صْغير → أَصْغَر; طَويل → أَطْوَل; قَصير → أَقْصَر; جْديد → أَجْدَد; قَديم → أَقْدَم; سَهِل → أَسْهَل; صَعِب → أَصْعَب
column4: The comparative has one form for both genders — it does not take ة.

column1: How do you form the comparative of an adjective ending in a vowel?
column2: Drop the final vowel, prefix ا, and end in ى (alif maqsoura).
column3: غالي → أَغْلى; حامي → أَحْمى; حِلْو → أَحْلى; ذَكي → أَذْكى; غَبي → أَغْبى
column4: These end in ى, not ي — أغلى, not أغلي.

column1: How do you say bigger than, and the biggest?
column2: Comparative + من for than. For the superlative, put the comparative directly before a singular noun.
column3: بَرْلين أَكْبَر مِن هامْبورْغ (Berlin is bigger than Hamburg); بَرْلين أَكْبَر مَدينِة بْألْمانْيا (Berlin is the biggest city in Germany); الحُمُّص أَطْيَب أَكِل عَرَبي
column4: The same word أكبر does both jobs — the structure after it tells you which one is meant.

column1: How do you talk about the future?
column2: Put رح before the present tense verb.
column3: نِحْنا رَح نْسافِر ع إسْبانْيا; رَح نْروح ع مَطْعَم سوري قَريب مِن هون
column4: رح is invariable — it never conjugates, only the verb after it does.

column1: How do you say something is happening right now?
column2: Put عم before the present tense verb. Negate with ما before عم.
column3: أَنا اِشْرَب (I drink) → أَنا عَم اِشْرَب (I'm drinking); اِنْتَ تِكْتُب → اِنْتَ عَم تِكْتُب; أَنا ما عَم اِدْرُس عَرَبي
column4: Without عم the present is a habit, not an action in progress.

column1: Which verbs never take عم?
column2: Verbs of motion, location and mental state. Use the active participle instead.
column3: motion: رايِح (going), راجِع (returning), مْسافِر (travelling), جاي (coming); mental state: نايِم (sleeping), فاهِم (understanding); location: عايِش / ساكِن (living), قاعِد (sitting)
column4: هو عم ينام is wrong — say هو نايم. The participle agrees like an adjective: نايم، نايمة، نايمين.

column1: What are the three negation words and when does each apply?
column2: لا negates commands. ما negates verbs in all other tenses. مو (or مش) negates nouns and adjectives.
column3: لا تْروح عَالبيت; ما بِدّي شي; ما عَم اِدْرُس; أَنا مو جوعان; هادا مو كْتاب
column4: مش and مو are interchangeable; مش is heard more in Palestinian and Lebanese speech.

column1: How do you attach an object pronoun to a verb?
column2: Add the possessive endings to the verb, except that me is ني rather than ي.
column3: شوفْني (see me), شوفَك، شوفَك، شوفْكُن، شوفْنا، شوفُه، شوفْها، شوفْهُن; اَعْطيني الشاي; خِدْني عَالبيت; إيمْتى بِدَّك تْشوفيني؟; كيف فيني ساعْدَك؟
column4: me is the one that breaks the pattern: ني on a verb versus ي on a noun.

column1: How do you say for me, for you, in order to?
column2: مشان plus the possessive endings. Before a verb it means in order to.
column3: مِشاني، مِشانَك، مِشانَك، مِشانْكُن، مِشانّا، مِشانو، مِشانْها، مِشانُن; هاي القَهْوِة مِشانَك; بِدّي روح ع ألْمانْيا مِشان اِشْتِغِل
column4: Same word covers for someone and in order to — the following word tells you which.

column1: What form does a counted noun take?
column2: Two of something takes the dual ين on the noun. Three to ten takes the plural. Eleven and above takes the singular.
column3: يومين (two days), سَيّارْتين (two cars); تْلات ساعات، خَمِس دَقايِق (plural); إيدَعْش يوم، عِشْرين سِنِة (singular)
column4: Going back to the singular after eleven feels wrong in English but is required in Arabic.

column1: When is the ة at the end of a word pronounced (a) instead of (eh)?
column2: When the letter before it is one of ج، ح، خ، ر، ز، ص، ض، ط، ظ، ع، ق.
column3: قَصيرِة (asiira), بِشْعَة (besh'a), رْخيصَة (rkhiisa), صْغيرَة (zghiira) — versus حِلْوِة (helwe), جْديدِة (jdiide), كْبيرَة (kbiire)
column4: This is the same rule the book states for its starred adjectives, here generalised to the whole letter set.

column1: How do you ask how long something has been going on?
column2: قدّيش صرلك plus عم and the present verb. Answer with صرلي and a duration.
column3: قَدّيش صَرْلَك عَم تِشْرَب قَهْوِة؟; صَرْلي عَم اِشْرَب قَهْوِة مِن خَمِس دَقايِق; صَرْلي بِالبيت تْلات ساعات
column4: صر takes possessive endings like a made-up verb: صرلي، صرلك، صرله.

column1: What is the difference between إيمتى and لمّا?
column2: إيمتى asks a question (when?). لمّا introduces a time clause inside a statement (when …).
column3: إيمْتى بِدَّك تْشوفيني؟; شو بِتْحِبّ تْساوي لَمَّا اِنْتَ فاضي؟
column4: Don't use إيمتى inside a statement. Note the book also uses بس for when in a clause.

column1: What is the difference between كم and قدّيش?
column2: كم asks how many and is followed by a singular noun. قدّيش asks how much, or how long.
column3: كَم أَخ وْإِخْت عِنْدَك؟; قَدّيش عُمْرَك؟; قَدّيش صَرْلَك هون؟
column4: كم takes a singular noun: كم أخ, not كم إخوة.
